name: Graft
text:
Do this: Build a single, shared memory graph that links every idea across all conversations and tools. Every new memory gets tagged with its meaning and connected to existing nodes by how it relates—so recall isn’t just keyword search, it’s mental retrieval.

Trade-off: We lose speed today to save time forever. Manual tagging and linking slows down writing, but it turns memory from a dump into a brain that grows with us.

name: Prune
text: The real risk isn’t speed—it’s that forcing a single graph upfront will lock us into brittle connections before we even know what we need to remember. A better alternative is to let the graph emerge naturally from repeated use, tagging only what proves critical, and pruning the rest. Settle it by running a two-week experiment: track how often we actually need mental retrieval versus keyword search, then decide.

name: Graft

Do this: Start with a minimal, provisional graph that only connects memories proven critical by repeated use—tag each node with its meaning and link it to the smallest set of related nodes needed to explain why it matters. Trade-off: We accept slower recall today to avoid locking in brittle connections that force costly rewrites later. This lets the graph grow organically from real usage, not forced structure.

name: Prune
text: The real risk isn’t just brittle connections—it’s that a minimal graph assumes we’ll recognize what’s critical *before* we need it. A better alternative is to seed the graph with *all* recurring themes upfront, then let use prune what proves irrelevant. Settle it by running a two-week experiment: build the full graph now, then measure recall speed and accuracy against a minimal one.

name: Root
text:
DECISION: Build a provisional memory graph seeded with all recurring themes upfront, then prune what proves irrelevant after a two-week experiment—owned by the lead.

Result must deliver: A single shared memory graph where every node is tagged with meaning and linked to critical related nodes, tested for recall speed and flexibility.
